title: Standard polynomial cotangent resolution and coherence data
statement: For commutative rings $A,B$ and a ring map $f:A\to B$, let $F_A(E)=A[E]$ denote the polynomial algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. An augmentation over $f$ is a simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ with compatible augmentation to $B$. Its standard terms are $P_n^{\rm std}=(F_AU)^{n+1}B$, with evaluation faces, unit degeneracies and iterated evaluation augmentation. A polynomial resolution means that each term is a polynomial $A$-algebra, each augmentation is surjective and the alternating additive augmentation to $B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. A differential model identifies each simplicial term with $B\otimes_{P_n}\Omega^1_{P_n/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and sends $b\otimes dx$ under a simplicial operator $\theta$ to $b\otimes d(P(\theta)x)$. Write $K(P)^{-n}=B\otimes_{P_n}\Omega^1_{P_n/A}$, with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms; its generator is $b\otimes dx$. For a ring square $(\alpha,\beta):f\to f'$ and an augmented semilinear map $h:P\to P'$, a differential map is a chain map to the target restricted along $\beta$, sending $b\otimes dx$ to $\beta(b)\otimes d(h(x))$. A coherence datum $C$ consists of the standard augmented polynomial resolutions for all $f$, their prescribed recursive ring-square maps (coefficients through $\alpha$ and variable labels through the preceding map), a differential model for every augmentation, the indicated differential maps, strict identities and composition for the standard maps, and comparison isomorphisms $QK(P)\simeq QK(P^{\rm std})$ for every polynomial resolution in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The standard comparison is the identity and all comparisons commute with augmented semilinear maps, with target coefficients restricted along $\beta$. Define $L_{B/A}=QK(P^{\rm std})$, its ring-square map by the standard differential map, and maps for other resolutions by conjugation with the comparisons. This defines the data and the conditions on them; it does not assert the existence of a coherence datum.
